intended_object: Lie(N) as an ideal of Lie(G). Here G is the affine group scheme Spec H over a commutative ring R, and N is the normal closed subgroup cut out by the normal Hopf ideal I. Lie(N) consists of the tangent vectors, i.e. the counit-derivations H → B, that vanish on I. It is an ideal of Lie(G) = Der_R(H, B_ε) (Milne, Algebraic Groups §10; Jantzen I.7). This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes the library's existing closed-subgroup Lie subalgebra `I.lieSubalgebra` and repackages its underlying submodule as a `LieIdeal`.

- **Elements.** `I.lieSubalgebra` is the range of the Lie hom induced by the quotient H → H/I. By `mem_lieSubalgebra_iff`, its elements are exactly the derivations d : H → B (along the counit) with d(I) = 0. This is the standard description of Lie(N) inside Lie(G).
- **Ideal property.** The bracket-closure field is supplied by the theorem `IsNormal.lie_mem_lieSubalgebra`, which proves from scheme-theoretic normality that ⁅d, e⁆ ∈ Lie(N) for every d ∈ Lie(G) and e ∈ Lie(N).
- **Supporting lemmas.** `mem_lieIdeal_iff` and `lieIdeal_toLieSubalgebra` confirm that membership means vanishing on I, as intended.

On generality: the setting is already broad. It works over any commutative base ring R, any commutative Hopf algebra H, and any commutative R-algebra B of coefficients, with no smoothness or finite-type assumptions. Mathlib has no Lie algebra of an affine group scheme, and no Lie ideal of a normal subgroup scheme, so there is nothing more general to compare against. The definition is faithful.
